newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries end near flat, Fed watch persists.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries end near flat, Fed watch persists.

text.p: Prices of U.S. Treasury securities ended little changed on Wednesday as players mulled prospects for Federal Reserve action on interest rates later this month.

Fears of a strong Beige Book and comments by Fed Governor Janet Yellen that rising labor costs could trigger inflation pushed Treasuries lower in early trade. Bond prices staged a comeback just after midday however, when the Fed report indicated inflation was under control and the economy continued to expand at a moderate pace.

"Inflation indicators .... were varied and generally inconclusive, although there appears to be greater upward pressure on wages than on prices," said the Beige Book summary prepared by the Cleveland Federal Reserve

"There was some relief that the Beige Book was not more pessimistic on the price front," said Kathy Bostjancic, money market analyst at UBS Securities Inc. "We had a relief trade and then some short covering."
The benchmark 6.75 percent 30-year Treasury bond closed unchanged at 95-17/32 to yield 7.11 percent. The 6.125 percent two-year note closed flat at 99-20/32 to yield 6.33 percent.

Traders got a fresh reminder of the Fed's worries about inflation when Yellen told the Washington Post, "I find myself nervous about the diminishing slack in the labor market. I think we are in an inflationary zone."
Yellen's remarks echoed comments published by Reuters on Tuesday.
Analysts said the market has priced in a Fed rate hike of 25 basis point, but this week's inflation data could change market expectations.

"If PPI and CPI come in tame, we could say we've got a chance at no (Fed) move," Jim Bianco, trader at Arbor Trading Group Inc, said. "Basically the marketplace by the way it traded today, has got their bet down and now they'll wait to see if CPI will change their perception of a Fed tightening." The Labor Department will release the August producer and consumer price reports on Thursday and Friday, respectively. Economists surveyed by Reuters expect overall and core producer prices to rise at a 0.1 percent pace in August. Consumer prices are seen rising 0.2 percent in both the overall and core readings.

"The market still has 25 priced in, and any expectations of 50 are starting to diminish and will disappear on benign (inflation) numbers," said Donald Maude, chief U.S. fixed income strategist at ScotiaMcLeod.

In another look at the economy, the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago said its newly revised and updated Chicago Fed Midwest Manufacturing Index rose 0.5 percent in July to a record high reading of 128.9. Analysts said the report moved the market marginally downward.
Three-month bill rates closed up 1/32 at 5.16 percent, six-month bill rates were off four basis points at 5.29 percent and year-bill rates were unchanged at 5.58 percent.
The Treasury's 6-1/2 percent five-year note also closed flat at 99-06/32 to yield 6.69 percent and its 7-percent 10-year note rose 1/32 to 100-17/32, yielding 6.92 percent.
